predecessors.name: German Africa
predecessors.text: the coast opposite Zanzibar round Bagamoyo, the first capital, where Peters' company treaties lay (the page gives no boundary)

successors.name: Tanganyika Territory
successors.text: the mainland of present Tanzania, 'Tanganyika' becoming the British territory's name on 10 January 1920

successors.name: Portuguese Mozambique
successors.text: the Kionga triangle on the Rovuma, 'virtually forced Portugal to cede the triangle in 1894'

ledger.x: 1885 (27 February): the German East Africa Company receives its imperial charter.
1888: the coast rises against the Company.
1889: the revolt is put down 'with British help the following year'.
1890 (1 July): the Heligoland-Zanzibar Treaty fixes the German sphere.
1897: Burundi joins Rwanda as a German district.
1914 (3 August): the East African campaign begins.
1916 (June): Belgian forces occupy Urundi ('Urundi in June 1916').
1916 (September): the British hold the Central Railway.
1918 (25 November): the East African campaign ends.
1919 (30 May): the Belgian occupation of Ruanda becomes a cession ('Britain ceded the north-western GEA districts of Ruanda and Urundi to Belgium').
1919 (30 May): the Belgian occupation of Urundi becomes a cession under the same Anglo-Belgian agreement.
1919 (30 May): Britain cedes Ruanda and Urundi to Belgium.

1919 (28 June): the British occupation of the Central Railway lands ends in the division of the colony (Treaty of Versailles of 28 June 1919, in force 10 January 1920); the lands become the Tanganyika mandate.
1919 (28 June): the British occupation of the south ends in the same division; 'Tanganyika' becomes the name of the British territory on 10 January 1920.
1919 (28 June): the colony is formally dissolved.

wars.name: East African campaign (World War I)
wars.outcome: Allied victory: Belgians in Ruanda and Urundi in 1916, the British on the Central Railway by September 1916, Lettow-Vorbeck into Mozambique on 23 November 1917 and surrender at Abercorn on 25 November 1918; the colony divided among Britain, Belgium and…

wars.name: Maji Maji Rebellion
wars.outcome: No border change; the page opened gives only the start (1905; 21 October 1905 on the infobox).

certainty.note: The German sphere's northern border with the East Africa Protectorate was fixed by the 1890 treaty but 'unsurveyed until 1910'; the 'exact boundaries remained unsurveyed'.
